plotSections.title: Walker's departure and Reach travel plan
bullets: Walker confirms Plymouth Gawater is with him before resuming play.
Walker uses his small portal cube to pop out in The Reach near the Whispering Abyss.
Sylan notes Walker can navigate by mind link and treats the outing as a short, low-risk adventure.
From the Whispering Abyss, Walker plans to fly north toward the Lost Isles to reach the Dragon Rider training grounds.
The DM places the training guild on the largest unnamed island in the hex between the Lost Islands, Camp Two, and the Howling tunnels.

Elrus previously said Last Word Chasm to the training grounds is about five days by flight; Walker initially estimated eight days, but the DM treats the straight-line route as essentially the same and settles on about five days.
Walker finalizes a broader 49-day itinerary in The Reach, spending five dragon energy per day for 245 total energy and accepting one exhaustion level per day for the full stay.
The DM confirms this plan can still be changed mid-journey and that Walker will have disadvantage on ability checks throughout unless he adjusts course.
Dragon-rider exhaustion has no reliable cure except labor-intensive potions; cleric or paladin magic can help, but Dana and Ord are not with Walker, and Elrus cannot cure exhaustion daily.
Nicotine can help short-term but causes harsh withdrawal without supply; Walker makes a mental note to acquire it after giving up alcohol.

plotSections.title: Sunder detour and group split
bullets: Walker plans to fly with Elrus and Plymouth toward the training grounds, routing over Sunder to shop for exhaustion relief.
The DM agrees Sunder may carry exhaustion potions and other rare supplies.
Elrus declines supplies, says he dislikes frequenting Sunder, and will meet Walker in the mountains with Araden.
Plymouth flies into Sunder with Walker while Elrus and Araden head for the mountains.
Glimmen waits outside shops while Walker goes inside.

plotSections.title: Communication while separated
bullets: Walker tells Ciri mind-link communication is open if she needs anything, though the DM notes mind chat is likely out of range without a spell.
Elrus's dragon could use fire bursts as a signal.
Elrus and Plymouth teach Walker rudimentary SOS fire signals and basic flag-communique recognition, but not as a proficiency.
Dragon-rider guild flags exist for ground observers to signal riders, not for riders to signal others.

plotSections.title: Arrival in Sunder
bullets: Sunder is a floating amalgamation of towers and islands in The Reach.
Named districts include Haven Hold at the center, the Bronze Palace, the Bronze Arena, Miss Mary's, the docks, the Prancing Fox, and Louise Casino.
The Haven may have exhaustion potions and magic items, some tied to completing another Sunder Chase circuit.
Haven Hold's dragon hoard is enchanted by Benji and that dragon so racers may pick from it before running the circuit.
Calypso runs a floating vending operation between Miss Mary's and the dock corridor.
The docks teem with griffins, giant eagles, flying ships, and a diverse market crowd; Walker draws fewer stares than usual for a dragon rider.
Plymouth is eager to visit several areas he has been eyeing.

plotSections.title: Qualin's Quax and shopping
bullets: Walker seeks potions or magic items to offset daily dragon-rider exhaustion; Plymouth seeks horn root, powdered dragon scale, wet alchemical items, and dragon gizzard for spell components.
Plymouth recommends greater restoration or a rare potion of vitality, though both are expensive in Sunder.
They buy herbs and raw ingredients from street vendors, then enter Qualin's Quax, a Sunder apothecary smelling of thyme, oleander, earthy root, and citrus.
The shopkeeper Quaylin is a stately duck-like Aarakocra in blue robes with purple trim, cataloging potions when they enter.
Plymouth negotiates dragon gizzard at five gold per pound while Walker fails a perception check with disadvantage from exhaustion and becomes fixated on Quaylin's heirloom gem.
Quaylin wears the Quackless of the Quinn's line, a family-heirloom purple gem valued at about five million gold and not for sale.
Quaylin shows four potions of vitality in a five-vial crate; each removes all exhaustion from a long adventuring day, cures poison and similar ailments, and improves the next short rest.
The fuchsia potions cost twelve hundred gold apiece and come with the Quax guarantee.
Walker is too worn down to haggle and cannot afford them.
Quaylin suggests Walker borrow liquid gold directly from the Haven Hold dragon at low interest without running another Sunder Chase.
Plymouth confirms he secured several pounds of dragon gizzard, and Walker leaves to speak with the dragon.

plotSections.title: Walker's gold hand origin
bullets: Quaylin taps Walker's gold-colored hand with a pestle and confirms it is real flesh, not metal for sale.
Walker says the change happened while swimming underwater in cold molten-looking water, possibly near the Temple of I in the north.
He put only his hand into the substance and it turned gold; he did not test anything else because he panicked.
Quaylin compares the result to a Midas-like alchemical process and asks whether loon folk were involved; Walker says no, and they share a mutual dislike of loon folk.
Plymouth silently signals Walker to stop discussing the incident in the shop.

plotSections.title: Invisible silent boat crisis
bullets: While Walker shops in Sunder, the main party remains invisible on the boat and unable to hear one another.
Closing the door left the ship floating in place; it can list side to side but is otherwise back to normal except for the invisibility and silence.
Ord's oily dragon-vessel outline is still faintly visible but has mostly dissipated.
A floating spectral door remains closed where the doorway was.
Gerk remains confused and largely unable to act normally.

plotSections.title: Cross-realm economics
bullets: Gerk asks whether gold has the same value across Atlas's realms.
The DM confirms exchange differences exist and notes the party has access to six of eight Arch realms.
The party could theoretically create a cross-realm market and exploit foreknowledge of keystone door openings to cause economic hardship against the lich.
Gerk jokingly names the market The Gerkin.

plotSections.title: Breaking Gerk's confusion
bullets: Sylan decides against reopening the spectral door now that the ship seems stabilized.
With no ship log available, Sylan writes detect magic on the deck using coins.
Sylan physically wrangles the invisible Gerk by slapping, grabbing, and shaking him under his chitin armor.
Gerk feels accosted, grabs back, and becomes slightly more lucid enough to recognize his boat and a smaller person's wrist in his grip.
Gerk fails a wisdom save with a natural 1 and tries to swing Sylan around in a strength contest.
Ciri watches the invisible struggle without being able to see what is happening.

plotSections.title: Ord casts See Invisibility
bullets: Ord, still outlined in oil from his dragon vessel, cannot communicate normally with the others.
Sylan asks whether the invisibility is magical; Ord does not have detect magic prepared but offers dispel magic instead.
Ord casts See Invisibility after covering himself in more oil.
The level-two divination lets Ord see invisible creatures and objects, including into the ethereal plane.
Ord sees Gerk half dazed on the deck wrestling with Sylan near the closed floating spectral door.
Dana stands nearby looking concerned and confused.
Two crew members, including the helmsman, wander the deck bumping into each other and silently trying to call out.
All interactions remain soundless despite visible movement.
Where Gerk opened the portal, Ord sees faint glowing edge-lines and ghostly city passerby that fade quickly and are nearly gone when he investigates.
Ord tries to steady Sylan and Gerk without restraining them; his persuasion check of 15 is enough that they notice his oily silhouette.

plotSections.title: Blind eye speech and door investigation
bullets: Sylan uses a token of blind eye speech to whisper with Ord and confirm he can see them through See Invisibility.
Gerk admits through the token that he opened the door.
The spectral door floats over and slightly behind Gerk, shut and frameless, resembling Gerk's shield-door but more functional.
With guidance, Gerk's investigation total of 18 reveals it is not a real door but protective magic with no portal or opening capability.
Gerk, Sylan, and Ord find their hands pass through it into slightly thicker air without physical effect.
The DM confirms passing through the spectral door would not simply restore sight or hearing.

plotSections.title: Dispel magic debate and resolution
bullets: Sylan says dispel magic may be the party's best available tool but warns about their poor track record with it.
The party fears dispelling the wrong effect could drop the ship; Dana is the one most likely able to prevent a fatal fall.
Ord proposes zone of truth as a workaround, but the group moves toward dispel magic instead.
Ord asks Gerk to create a replacement door as Doorman, but Gerk refuses to listen to Ord and briefly suggests leaving through a new magic door instead.
Sylan insists they cannot abandon the boat because it is too important.
The party recalls a past dispel during the Sunder Chase that went badly.
Sylan casts guidance on Ord while Ord targets the magical effect impeding sight and hearing, not the boat or its wings.
Ord's dispel magic succeeds and sound returns; the entire party can see and hear one another again.
Confused crew members become visible; one had been screaming while another clung to the banister.
The spectral door remains floating in the sky, but the party still cannot use it.
The party praises Ord for breaking the silence and invisibility effect.

plotSections.title: Head count and moving on
bullets: Sylan calls for a head count to make sure no one fell off during the muted invisible episode.
All four named crew members are found safe aboard; none jumped or fell off.
Ciri hides behind the mast or a barrel and is eventually accounted for.
Walker is not on the boat; he is away on his separate Sunder mission.
Mikkel the spymaster is not aboard again, continuing the recurring problem of departing without him.
The party discusses giving Mikkel a sending stone or teleportation tunnel so he can rejoin more reliably.
Sylan offers Dana about thirty minutes to investigate the spectral door, but Dana's player is absent and Dana lacks investigative spells such as detect magic.
The party decides not to wait and continues the journey as if nothing happened.
The party agrees not to open doors on moving things again.

plotSections.title: Spectral door follows Gerk
bullets: As the ship resumes travel, the fake spectral door continues following Gerk rather than staying fixed in the sky.
It keeps roughly the same distance from Gerk as he moves around the ship.
When the ship sails forward, the door remains stationary relative to the ship, as if standing on it.
Gerk tries waving, verbal commands, closed sesame, and a performance check totaling 17 to dismiss it; nothing works.
Sylan tells Gerk he may keep experimenting but must not open another door until they reach land.

plotSections.title: Walker meets Hanzuni at Haven Hold
bullets: Walker has only about fourteen hundred gold on hand—826 gold and 61 platinum—while roughly ten thousand gold remains back in Langdale.
Walker enters Haven Hold's hoard hall: a lively arched market with a treasure mountain on a central floating island separated by an empty moat.
Throwing a gauntlet into the hoard triggers a Sunder Chase; the hoard's magic keeps treasure from falling away.
Hanzuni is an ancient copper dragon (H-A-Z-U-N-I), relatively small for his age, with polished copper scales; he swims through his hoard.
He greets Glimmen first, remembers her as a hatchling, and has forgotten Walker's name.
Glimmen eagerly dives into the hoard to swim with him; Hanzuni is only slightly larger than her despite his ancient age.
Walker asks Hanzuni for something to remedy terrible daily exhaustion despite constant training.
Hanzuni perceives shimmering magical energy on Walker and criticizes his mismatched star sapphire and star ruby earrings.
He offers an even-value hoard trade for matching gems; Walker refuses to keep the story of gems won from a past dragon hoard fight.

plotSections.title: Quaylin's backstory
bullets: Hanzuni confirms Quaylin of Quaylin's Quax and says Quaylin has won two Sunder Chases.
Quaylin was not always a duck-fowl; the Beak of the quackiest of brews transmutes the wearer and grants great potion knowledge.
The neck heirloom is his prize from his second Sunder Chase win; the beak relates to his first.
Quaylin arrived in Sunder after his race on a small vessel with only potion craft to his name.

plotSections.title: Walker's plated gold hand at Haven Hold
bullets: Hanzuni says many hoard items could cure exhaustion, but removing magical items requires a Sunder Chase.
Walker cannot remove his golden hand to throw into the hoard.
Hanzuni grabs it and slides off a perfect golden replica, revealing Walker's normal flesh hand beneath.
It is not a gauntlet but plated gold; Hanzuni returns it and Walker can reattach it like a perfect-fitting glove.
Hanzuni estimates it weighs roughly thirty pounds, or about four hundred troy ounces of gold.
Walker is unsettled to learn it can come off; Hanzuni says many people do not realize it is only plated.

plotSections.title: Sunder Chase rules
bullets: Participants choose as many magical hoard items as they wish, then must race.
Items lost overboard during the race return to the hoard; non-winners lose all taken items back to the hoard.
Only the winner's chosen treasures permanently leave Hanzuni's hoard.
Walker wants to compete but lacks time; Sylan notes retrieving gold from Midgar would be faster.

plotSections.title: Hanzuni's gold loan
bullets: Hanzuni can loan plain gold from the hoard but cannot give magical items such as a potion of vitality directly.
His interest is not monetary; he charges a quest because he cannot leave the hoard unattended.
For the price of Quaylin's twelve-hundred-gold potion, he asks Walker to bring him an island crab, which he has not eaten in a long time.
Hanzuni tips that Quaylin favors alabaster herring, especially pickled, and may haggle down a few hundred gold.

Walker says he cannot afford the potions and is too tired to haggle.

Walker explains he turned his hand gold by putting it into cold molten-looking water while swimming, possibly near the Temple of I.
Plymouth signals Walker to stop talking about the gold hand.
Walker and Quaylin discuss loon folk.
Plymouth confirms he bought several pounds of dragon gizzard.
Walker leaves Qualin's Quax to negotiate with the Haven Hold dragon.
The scene shifts to the main party, still invisible and unable to hear each other on the boat.
Sylan notes they can still see a faint oily outline of Ord, which is fading.
Gerk remains confused and unable to act.
The party discusses cross-realm gold value and the possibility of exploiting Arch-realm trade against the lich.
Sylan notes the floating spectral door is now closed.
The DM confirms the ship is floating in place and otherwise back to normal aside from invisibility and silence.
Sylan writes detect magic on the floor with coins.

Gerk grabs back and becomes slightly more lucid.
Gerk fails a wisdom save.
Gerk tries to swing Sylan around during the struggle.
Ciri watches the invisible chaos without being able to see it.
Ord determines he does not have detect magic prepared but does have dispel magic.
Ord casts See Invisibility while covered in oil.
Ord sees Gerk and Sylan wrestling near the closed spectral door, with Dana and confused crew nearby in silent motion.
Ord notices fading glowing lines and ghostly city figures where Gerk opened the portal.
Ord investigates the fading lines, but they are nearly gone by the time he arrives.
Ord steadies Sylan and Gerk with a persuasion check of 15.
Sylan uses a token of blind eye speech to whisper with Ord.
Gerk says he opened the door.
Gerk sees the shut floating spectral door behind him.
Gerk investigates the door with guidance and totals 18.
Gerk learns the spectral door is fake protective magic, not a real portal.
Gerk, Sylan, and Ord find their hands pass through the spectral door without effect.
Gerk wildly swings through the door to no avail.
Ord tries and fails to grasp the spectral doorknob.
The party debates using dispel magic and fears the ship could fall.
Ord proposes zone of truth as a truthful-ideas workaround.
Ord commits to casting dispel magic on the magical effect impeding sight and hearing, explicitly not on the boat.
Ord asks Gerk to create a replacement door as Doorman; Gerk refuses and briefly proposes leaving through a new magic door instead.
Sylan insists they must stay with the boat.
Sylan casts guidance on Ord.
Ord casts dispel magic on the magical effect impeding sight and hearing.
The dispel succeeds and the party regains sight and sound.
The crew reappear, confused after trying to communicate silently.
Gerk confirms the spectral door is still present but unusable.
The party congratulates Ord and jokes about him being covered in oil.
Sylan calls for a head count while the boat is still in flight.
All four crew members are found safe aboard.
Ciri is located hiding behind the mast or a barrel.
Sylan confirms Mikkel is not aboard the boat.
Sylan says Gerk caused the incident and offers Dana thirty minutes to investigate the spectral door.
The party skips waiting for Dana because she is absent and lacks investigative spells such as detect magic.
The party continues travel, pretending nothing happened.
The spectral door begins following Gerk and stays fixed on the ship as it moves.
Gerk fails to dismiss the door through physical, verbal, and performance attempts.
Sylan forbids Gerk from opening another door until they reach land.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen, Gatekeeper of The Reach.
notes: Is traveling with Plymouth Gawater on a short side excursion, using a portal cube to exit into The Reach near the Whispering Abyss.
Plans a multi-day dragon flight north to the Dragon Rider training grounds, with a broader 49-day Reach stay at five dragon energy per day for 245 total energy and one exhaustion level per day.
Will operate at disadvantage on ability checks for the trip unless he changes course.
Has given up alcohol and considers nicotine as a short-term replacement vice after learning it can help with exhaustion.
Is flying with Elrus and Plymouth toward the training grounds via a detour over Sunder to shop for exhaustion relief.
Learns basic SOS fire signals and simple flag-communique recognition, but not as a proficiency; usually relies on mind messages from Dana instead.
Opens mind-link communication with Ciri while separated.
Fails a perception check with disadvantage in Qualin's Quax and becomes fixated on Quaylin's heirloom gem.
Cannot afford twelve hundred gold per potion of vitality and is too exhausted to haggle.
Decides to seek a loan from the Haven Hold dragon rather than run another Sunder Chase.
Has a gold-colored hand that is real flesh, not metal; Quaylin tested it with a pestle.
Believes the hand turned gold when he put it into cold molten-looking water while swimming underwater, possibly near the Temple of I in the north.
Has about 826 gold and 61 platinum on hand while roughly ten thousand gold remains in Langdale.
Seeks Hanzuni at Haven Hold for a loan, gift, or affordable magical item to treat worsening daily exhaustion.
Tells Hanzuni that Quaylin sent him.
Wears mismatched star sapphire and star ruby earrings from a past dragon hoard fight and declines Hanzuni's offer to trade for matching gems.
His golden hand is plated gold, not a gauntlet, and can be removed as a solid replica weighing about thirty pounds.
Cannot throw the gold hand into the hoard to trigger a Sunder Chase.
Declines a Sunder Chase due to time pressure and accepts Hanzuni's quest-based gold loan terms.
personality: Pragmatic about enduring exhaustion for the mission.
Recently gave up alcohol and is looking for a replacement vice.
Easily distracted by valuable gems when exhausted.
Sometimes acts first and thinks later when curious.
quotesThemes: Mental note. Get nicotine.
I dropped the booze. I need a vice, guys.
I'm here for items or potions or anything to help me with just being tired.
I suffer from exhaustion all the time.
Of course I put my hand in it because it was cold molten stuff.
openQuestions: What would you say this gold hand is worth?

notes: Is present with Walker for this Reach excursion and flies into Sunder with him while Elrus and Araden head for the mountains.
Seeks horn root, powdered dragon scale, wet alchemical items, and dragon gizzard for spell components.
Knows Sunder's market well enough to lead Walker through street vendors to Qualin's Quax.
Recommends greater restoration or a rare potion of vitality for Walker's exhaustion.
Negotiates dragon gizzard at five gold per pound while Walker is distracted.
Signals Walker to stop explaining his gold hand in front of Quaylin.
Secured several pounds of dragon gizzard from Quaylin.
personality: Talkative and eager in the Sunder market.
Knowledgeable about alchemical supplies and exhaustion remedies.

Dragon Rider Training Grounds.existing: Dragon Rider guild training grounds near the Lost Isles.
notes: Located on the largest unnamed island in the relevant Reach hex, between the Lost Islands, Camp Two, and the Howling tunnels.
About five days of dragon flight from the Whispering Abyss under the travel time agreed in session.
Remains Walker's destination after a planned stop in Sunder.

notes: Walker and Plymouth pop out here when Walker uses his portal cube.

The training guild destination lies in a hex containing the Lost Islands, Camp Two, and the Howling tunnels.
Walker's current excursion is planned as a 49-day stay with daily exhaustion from dragon-energy use.

Cannot cure Walker's daily exhaustion.
Dislikes frequenting Sunder and declines supply purchases.
Helps teach Walker rudimentary fire signals before splitting off.

Not for sale. Family heirloom.
If it quacks or if it cracks, you can bring it back and you get your money back.
I fucking hate loon folk.
Come back later. We might have a sale on these.

notes: Purple heirloom gem of the Quinn's line worn by Quaylin.
Not for sale; Quaylin says it would take about five million gold to part with it.
Walker estimates it as comparable in value to star gems and other valuable couturements he carries.
Small Sunder apothecary shop with a doubly punned name.
Smells of thyme, oleander, earthy root, and citrus.
Sells dragon gizzard by the pound, potions of vitality, and other alchemical goods.
Offers the Quax guarantee on purchases.
Follows Walker through Sunder and waits outside while he enters shops.
Is present beside Walker at Haven Hold.
Eagerly dives into Hanzuni's hoard when invited to swim.
Hanzuni remembers her as a hatchling and notes she is now fully grown with a rider.
Is roughly similar in size to Hanzuni, who is only slightly larger.
personality: Excited and antsy when offered a swim in treasure.

notes: Fuchsia-toned potion resembling a greater healing potion.
Removes all exhaustion from a long day of adventuring.
Also cures poison and similar ailments such as snake bites or basilisk effects.
Improves healing on the next short rest.
Costs twelve hundred gold apiece at Qualin's Quax; four remain in stock.
Northern temple pronounced like the letter I.
Walker believes his gold-hand incident may have happened during time spent there.
openQuestions: Did Walker's gold hand originate at the Temple of I?

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian Doorman and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: Remains on the invisible, silent party boat under the confusion effect.
Feels accosted by unseen hands, grabs back, and becomes slightly more lucid.
Fails a wisdom save with a natural 1 and tries to swing Sylan around during the struggle.
Admits through blind eye speech that he opened the door.
Investigates the spectral door with guidance for a total of 18 and identifies it as fake protective magic.
Cannot physically interact with the spectral door beyond passing through it.
Refuses to listen to Ord's suggestion to create a replacement door and briefly proposes leaving through a new magic door instead.
Is blamed for causing the doorway incident on the moving boat.
Accepts the lesson not to open doors on moving things.
The spectral door now follows him, staying near him as he moves and fixed on the ship when it sails.
Waving, commands, closed sesame, and a 17 performance check fail to dismiss it.
Agrees not to open another door until the party reaches land.
Suggests giving Mikkel a teleportation tunnel or other way back to the boat.
personality: Distrusts Ord's suggestions in the moment.
quotesThemes: I opened door.
Oh wait guys, we can just leave. We can just go through a magic door and a new magic door.
Good job, Ord.
Guys, it's following me.
Go away door. We don't want you here.

Lich.existing: An unidentified lich whose phylactery may be hidden among his chess pieces.
notes: The DM says the party could use cross-realm trade and foreknowledge of keystone door openings to cause economic hardship against the lich.

Keystones.existing: Magical stones used to open and connect Atlas's Arch realms.
notes: The party currently has access to six of Atlas's eight Arch realms, enough to manipulate inter-realm trade if they choose.

Spectral Door.existing: A mysterious spectral door resembling Gerk's shield form.
notes: Floats over and slightly behind Gerk, fully shut and frameless, resembling his shield-door but more functional.
Investigation confirms it is fake protective magic with no real opening function.
Hands pass through it into slightly thicker air without physical effect; passing through does not restore sight or hearing.
Remains present and unusable after Ord's dispel magic on the sight-and-hearing effect.
Continues to follow Gerk after travel resumes, staying near him and fixed on the ship when it moves.
Remains non-interactable despite Gerk's attempts to dismiss it.

Confusion Effect.existing: A spell effect that leaves its victim confused and unable to act meaningfully.
notes: Still afflicts Gerk despite Sylan's physical attempts to shake him out of it.
Gerk fails a wisdom save with a natural 1 during the attempt.

dragon vessel.existing: A dragon vessel that outlines Ord's invisible body with olive oil.
notes: Ord is still covered in oil from the vessel and adds more oil on himself while casting See Invisibility.
Level-two divination spell Ord casts on himself.
Lets him see invisible creatures and objects, including ghostly translucent forms on the ethereal plane.
Lets Ord perceive the full silent scene on the boat.

Abel.existing: Surviving-and-revived crew member and the boat's helmsman.
notes: Visible to Ord as one of two confused crew members silently wandering the deck.
Is confirmed safe aboard with the other crew after the dispel.

Doorway.existing: A fixed supernatural passage between locations.
notes: Gerk's opened portal left fading glowing edge-lines and ghostly city visions separate from the floating spectral door.
That residue is nearly gone by the time Ord inspects it.
Opening a doorway on the moving boat caused the invisibility and silence effect.
The party agrees Gerk must not open another door until they reach land.
Sylan uses it to whisper with Ord when normal speech fails.
Requires pointing and whispering to activate.
Gerk can reply to whispers sent to him without needing to activate it himself.
Spymaster crew member who is not aboard again when the party checks.
The party has a recurring problem of departing without verifying he is onboard.
Party considers a sending stone or teleportation tunnel so he can rejoin.
Sunder district containing a dragon hoard at its center.
Hoard hall is a lively arched market with treasure on a central floating island separated by an empty moat.
Throwing a gauntlet into the hoard triggers a Sunder Chase.
Hoard magic prevents treasure from falling away and replenishes spilled coins.
Plain gold can pass out of the hoard by loan, but magical items cannot leave without a Sunder Chase win.
Ancient copper dragon (H-A-Z-U-N-I); male.
One of two ancient copper dragons Walker has met on The Reach.
Relatively small for an ancient dragon, with polished copper scales from swimming in his hoard.
Less tarnished than Araden due to constant activity in treasure.
Swims through his hoard at Haven Hold and offers low-interest loans repaid as quests.
Greets Glimmen before Walker and has forgotten Walker's name.
Perceives shimmering magical energy on Walker and criticizes his mismatched earrings.
Says magical hoard items that could cure exhaustion require a Sunder Chase to remove.
Can physically remove Walker's plated gold hand and identifies it as pure gold plating weighing roughly thirty pounds or four hundred troy ounces.
Has grown bored waiting for another Sunder Chase since Walker's last race.
Offers twelve hundred gold in exchange for an island crab.
Knows Quaylin may haggle if offered pickled alabaster herring.
personality: Playful and fond of swimming in treasure.
Fashion-conscious and eager for Sunder Chase excitement.
quotesThemes: Have you come for a swim, my dear?
All you need to do is take that golden gauntlet off your hand and throw it into the hoard.
What I charge is the quest.

Midgar.existing: Midgar realm and Arch of Atlas.
notes: Sylan suggests Walker could teleport there to retrieve his stored gold faster than running a Sunder Chase alone.

newTerms.name: Alabaster herring
notes: Pickled alabaster herring may help haggle Quaylin down on potion prices by a few hundred gold.

newTerms.name: Beak of the quackiest of brews
notes: Magical beak heirloom that transmutes the wearer into a duck-fowl and grants great potion knowledge.
Quaylin's prize from his first Sunder Chase win; his neck heirloom came from his second.

newTerms.name: Bronze Arena
notes: Named Sunder district, likely tied to Sunder Chase events.

newTerms.name: Bronze Palace
notes: Named Sunder district or landmark.

newTerms.name: Calypso
notes: Sunder vendor with a floating vending operation between Miss Mary's and the dock corridor.

newTerms.name: Camp Two
notes: Reach map landmark in the hex containing the Dragon Rider training guild island.

newTerms.name: Cross-realm trade manipulation
notes: With access to six of eight Arch realms, the party could build a cross-realm market and exploit keystone door-opening timing for economic leverage against the lich.

newTerms.name: Dragon energy points
notes: Walker's dragon-riding resource; spending five energy adds one level of exhaustion, rounded down.

newTerms.name: Dragon gizzard
notes: Alchemical spell component Plymouth seeks; Qualin's Quax sells it by the pound at five gold when in stock.

newTerms.name: Fake spectral door
notes: The floating spectral door is protective magic, not a real portal Gerk can open or close.
It follows Gerk after travel resumes and remains fixed on the ship when it moves.

newTerms.name: Fire signals
notes: Dragon-rider communication using flame bursts; Walker learned a basic SOS equivalent but not full proficiency.

newTerms.name: Flag signaling
notes: Non-magical ground-to-rider communication; guild flags are for observers to signal dragon riders, not for riders to signal others.

newTerms.name: Hanzuni
notes: Ancient copper dragon (H-A-Z-U-N-I) at the center of Haven Hold's hoard.
Known to Walker; offers low-interest gold loans repaid as quests rather than monetary interest.
Magical hoard items require winning a Sunder Chase to remove permanently.

newTerms.name: Haven Hold
notes: Central Sunder district housing Hanzuni's dragon hoard, enchanted as a Sunder Chase prize.
Throwing a gauntlet into the hoard triggers a chase; hoard magic replenishes spilled treasure.

newTerms.name: Horn root
notes: Alchemical ingredient Plymouth seeks in Sunder.

newTerms.name: Howling tunnels
notes: Reach map landmark bordering the hex with the training guild island.

newTerms.name: Island crab
notes: Delicacy Hanzuni wants Walker to fetch as repayment for a twelve-hundred-gold loan.

newTerms.name: Loon folk
notes: Aquatic people Quaylin strongly dislikes.
He asks whether they were involved in Walker's gold-hand incident.

newTerms.name: Louise Casino
notes: Named Sunder location.

newTerms.name: Mikkel
notes: Crew spymaster who is frequently left behind when the boat departs.

newTerms.name: Miss Mary's
notes: Named Sunder location near Calypso's vending route.

newTerms.name: Nicotine
notes: In-world stimulant that can help short-term with exhaustion but causes severe withdrawal without a steady supply.

newTerms.name: Plated gold hand
notes: Walker's golden hand is removable plated gold weighing about thirty pounds, not a gauntlet or permanently transformed flesh.
Hanzuni can slide it off as a solid replica, revealing Walker's normal hand beneath.

newTerms.name: Portal residue
notes: Fading glowing edge-lines and ghostly city visions left where Gerk opened his doorway, separate from the fake spectral door.

newTerms.name: Potion of vitality
notes: Rare fuchsia potion resembling a greater healing potion.
Removes all exhaustion from a long adventuring day, cures poison-like ailments, and improves the next short rest.
Quaylin sells them for twelve hundred gold apiece at Qualin's Quax; four remain in a five-vial crate.

newTerms.name: Prancing Fox
notes: Named Sunder district.

newTerms.name: Qualin's Quax
notes: Doubly named Sunder apothecary shop run by Quaylin.
Sells dragon gizzard, potions of vitality, and other alchemical goods with the Quax guarantee.

newTerms.name: Quax guarantee
notes: Qualin's Quax refund policy: if a purchased item quacks or cracks, the buyer gets their money back.

newTerms.name: Quaylin
notes: Duck-like Aarakocra proprietor of Qualin's Quax in Sunder.
Wears the Quackless heirloom; has won two Sunder Chases and was not always a duck-fowl.

newTerms.name: Salt leaf
notes: Supply Walker offered to buy for Elrus during the Sunder stop.

newTerms.name: See Invisibility
notes: Level-two divination that lets Ord see invisible creatures and objects, including ethereal forms.

newTerms.name: Sunder
notes: Floating Reach city of towers and islands with major market districts and rare alchemical goods.
Elrus dislikes visiting it often.

newTerms.name: Temple of I
notes: Northern temple pronounced like the letter I; Walker suspects it is connected to his gold hand.

newTerms.name: The Gerkin
notes: Joking name Gerk proposes for a cross-realm stock market using the party's keystone access.

newTerms.name: The Quackless
notes: Quaylin's family-heirloom purple gem of the Quinn's line.
Worth about five million gold and not for sale.

newTerms.name: Token of blind eye speech
notes: Magic item Sylan uses by pointing and whispering to communicate with another holder when normal speech fails.

newTerms.name: Whisper Master
notes: Sylan's nickname for Ciri during the head count.
